Data and storage

Where SATOM keeps its data — PostgreSQL, the device configuration cache and versioned source-of-truth store, the metrics store, the files under data/ — and how each one is replicated, retained and backed up.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced user
📍 WhereServer side — PostgreSQL database, /opt/satom/data/, /var/lib/satom-metrics/
On this page
  • Overview
  • The device configuration cache
  • The versioned source of truth (SoT)
  • The metrics store
  • The data directory
  • File permissions
  • Backups
  • Schema and migrations

Overview#

Store Holds Location Replicated to the standby by
PostgreSQL Users, profiles, appliances, settings, audit, jobs ledger rows, scheduled actions, change requests, the device cache, the SoT version index local database streaming replication
data/ Files: SoT blobs, latest per-device JSON, backups, job state, PKI shared slot, logs… /opt/satom/data/ satom-ha-datasync rsync every 5 min (most subdirectories)
Metrics store Time series for fleet metrics /var/lib/satom-metrics/ not replicated (each node keeps its own)
Redis (optional) Rate-limit counters, shared JSON cache memory not replicated

PostgreSQL is the source of truth for everything the application manages. In production the connection string comes from SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI in .env (see Configuration files); connections are checked before use and recycled every 30 minutes.

The device configuration cache#

Pages read device configuration from the local cache, not from the appliance. Contacting the appliance is an explicit action (refresh, sync, save).

Table Content
device_snapshots One row per device, layer and section capture
device_objects Every object and sub-object of every device, as JSON (JSONB on PostgreSQL), children linked by parent_id
device_server_policies, device_server_pools, device_web_protection_profiles Typed projections of the most used object types, rebuilt on every ingest
sync_runs One row per refresh
resource_locks Lease-based locks
inventory_snapshots Inventory captures

A configuration sweep that returns zero objects for a device is treated as an error and the cache is kept; a sweep aborts after several consecutive device-level errors rather than overwrite good data.

The versioned source of truth (SoT)#

NAF block: Observability. Despite its name, the Source of Truth is the history of each appliance's actual configuration — what the framework calls Observability. The desired state (NAF's Intent) is the Template library. See Where SATOM sits in the NAF Framework.

Each harvest also writes the device configuration as a snapshot:

  • data/reports/<device>/_config.json — the latest configuration, human readable.
  • data/sot/objects/<aa>/<sha256>.json.gz — content-addressed, gzip-compressed versions, indexed by the sot_version table.
  1. 1Harvestdevice configuration snapshot
  2. 2Canonicalisesort keys; strip volatile fields (timestamps, per-sweep errors, the appliance clock)
  3. 3HashSHA-256 of the canonical form
  4. 4Unchanged?only last_seen_at is advanced — no new blob, no new row
  5. 5Changedblob written under data/sot/objects/, sot_version row added
  6. 6Retentionolder payload moved to the backup server, then removed locally

The full snapshot is always stored; stripping only affects the hash, so diff and restore see exactly what the appliance returned. History, structural diff and restore are on the System backup page.

Setting (Settings → Configuration SoT) Default Meaning
Newest versions kept locally 2 per device Always kept on this node regardless of age
Days of payload kept locally 1 Payload younger than this also stays (the two rules are a union)
Days of change log kept in the database 365 Whole past months of sot_version rows are written to the backup server as JSONL, then removed here; 0 disables trimming

Each value can be set for all ADOMs (house rule) or per ADOM. Payload is deleted locally only after the backup server confirms it holds it; opening an evacuated version fetches it back automatically.

ℹ️Note — Git no longer stores device configuration

The per-device history used to be committed to git hourly. That was retired; git now carries application code only, and the satom-git-publish timer is no longer installed.

The metrics store#

Fleet metrics go to a local VictoriaMetrics instance (satom-metrics.service):

Setting Value
Listen address 127.0.0.1:8428 (loopback only — the store has no authentication)
Data directory /var/lib/satom-metrics (outside data/ on purpose)
Retention 396d
Memory cap 512MiB
Maximum query duration 30s

Boards, panels, collection targets and reports are configuration and stay in PostgreSQL. The store lives outside data/ because the HA sync rsyncs data/ with --delete, and a time-series database must not be rsynced while running. A node added to a pair builds its own history from the moment it starts collecting. See Metrics.

The data directory#

Everything below is under /opt/satom/data/ (owned by the service account, mode 0750; the service account's group has no other members, so no other local account can enter it).

Path Content
reports/ Latest per-device configuration JSON
sot/ Versioned configuration blobs
backups/ Per-appliance configuration-backup vault (indexed by config_backups)
system_backups/ System backup bundles (fmw-backup-<timestamp>.tar.gz)
git-bundles/ git bundle copies of the application repository
jobs/ One JSON file per background job (<id>.json)
deep_jobs/ Deep-capture job state
rediscovery/ Rediscovery runs
artifacts/ WAF artifacts
api_matrix/, field_schemas/ API library and field-schema data
imports/ Imported backup files, per device
firmware/ Uploaded firmware images
signatures.json Cached signature database
update-requests/, update-status/ Queue and results of the privileged runner
update-uploads/ Uploaded offline update packages
lib-versions/ Library version history (for rollback)
integrations/ Integration hooks: hooks/, queue/, claimed/, status/
pki-shared/ Node certificate published for the peer node
acme/ ACME account keys
cert-renew-archive/ Certificate renewal journal archive
recovery/seal.json Passphrase-sealed recovery envelope (if created)
branding/ Uploaded brand assets
known_hosts Pinned SSH host keys
ha_nodes.json HA node list
publication-rules.local.json Documentation redaction overlay
logs/satom.log Application error log (rotating)
diagnostics/, flight/, tmp/ Diagnostics, pre/post-flight baselines, scratch space

The HA sync excludes jobs/, tmp/, update-requests/, update-status/, logs/, diagnostics/ and deep_jobs/ — those are node-local. It copies with rsync -a, so the standby receives the same file modes as the primary.

File permissions#

The service runs with UMask=0022 on purpose (nginx must read the ACME webroot), so the protection is in the directory modes rather than the umask:

Path Directories Files
data/ itself 0750 —
backups/, system_backups/, acme/, recovery/, pki-shared/ and everything under them 0700 0600
  • The device config vault writes 0600 files in 0700 directories and narrows a vault directory an older release left open on its next write.
  • System bundles are 0600 from creation, written through a private file descriptor that refuses a symbolic link; a bundle fetched back from the backup server is written the same way.
  • satom diagnose data (also part of satom diagnose all) fails when data/ is looser than 0750 or anything in those trees is readable by group or other; sudo satom execute repair data --yes narrows them (without --yes it only prints the plan). The update runner runs the same repair after every update and the installer applies the modes on install. See CLI.

💡Tip — Scratch space

Nothing prunes data/tmp/ automatically. satom execute repair tmp deletes aged scratch files; satom execute repair jobs sweeps ghost jobs and prunes the job ledger. See CLI.

Backups#

Copy Mechanism Typical lag
This node Harvest writes data/reports/ and data/sot/ —
Standby PostgreSQL streaming + data/ rsync seconds / up to 5 min
External backup server SFTP push of SoT payload and system bundles up to 24 h
Downloadable bundle System Backup & Restore on demand

A system backup bundle contains:

  • db.dump — pg_dump of the database (custom format);
  • reports/ and sot/ (when reports are included);
  • recovery-seal.json — the sealed recovery envelope, if one exists;
  • config/ — the documentation redaction overlay;
  • manifest.txt — label, timestamp, database name and fingerprints of the recovery secrets.

FERNET_KEY and the internal CA key are not in the bundle. Restoring onto a rebuilt node needs them from the recovery envelope or from an export; the manifest fingerprints let a restore name a key mismatch. Restore takes a safety dump first, then runs pg_restore --clean. When a bundle is pushed to the backup server and verified (same name and size), older local bundles can be removed automatically. See System backup and, for appliance configuration backups, Backups.

Schema and migrations#

Each node builds its schema in two ways: at start-up db.create_all() plus additive column back-fills, and flask db upgrade (Alembic, migrations/) when an update runs. Because an installed node already has every table when Alembic first runs, migrations use idempotent helpers (app/migration_guard.py) that skip operations whose target already exists — they are not a start-up check.

Advanced Redis

Flask-Limiter stores counters in RATELIMIT_STORAGE_URI (default memory://, per worker). The JSON cache (app/services/cache.py, keys prefixed fmcache:) uses CACHE_REDIS_URI, or the rate limiter's URI when it is redis://, and falls back to an in-process cache when Redis is unreachable, retrying every 30 seconds. Nothing persistent lives in Redis.

Advanced Job files

Job state is written atomically (temporary file + rename) so a status poll on any gunicorn worker sees a consistent view. Status values are listed in Statuses.
